function.name: send_algorithm

content:
OK. Algorithm saved as algorithms/pivot_transpose.js and sent to Max (pivot_transpose).
Transformer, checked on a built-in test score: the roll is empty or Max did not hand it over (14 notes). In Max its source lives in memory (non-destructive: every run starts again from it).
Parameters (now a panel in Max):
  gap: slider 50..2000 ms = 300
  pivotNote: slider 1..64 = 3
  target: slider 1200..12700 mc = 6000
  register: range 1200..12700 mc = [1200,12700]
Checked in 7 runs (every slider at its minimum and maximum, every option).
Score at the declared values (14 notes, 1 ms):
voice 1 (Flute): 10 notes in 10 chords, 0-6100 ms, pitch 5600-6650
voice 2 (Cello): 4 notes in 3 chords, 0-6100 ms, pitch 5300-6000

Sent. The panel now has **gap** (phrase segmentation), **pivotNote** (which note of each phrase, by index from 1, anchors the shift), **target** (the pitch that pivot lands on — same for every phrase), and **register** (octave fold so notes stay in range). Every phrase is transposed as a block: the whole phrase moves by `target − pivotNote`, preserving its internal intervals.

based on the actual score segment by phrase in groups and do an algorithm that allows to transpose the whole phrase using any note of the phrase as a pivot note and setting a target pitch. The pivot note and the target pitch apply for all segments. So for example we can use the first note of every segment as a pivot note and set it to E4. This means that all phrases will have their first note at E4. If we set the third note as a pivot note and target pitch at G3 all phrases will transpose their structure so that their third note is G3. If the pivot note is out of range of the group (the pivot note is the 7th note and the phrase has only 6 notes...) the last note is used as pivot.

content:
OK. Algorithm saved as algorithms/pivot_transpose.js and sent to Max (pivot_transpose).
Transformer, checked on the score in the roll (893 notes). In Max its source lives in memory (non-destructive: every run starts again from it).
Parameters (now a panel in Max):
  gap: slider 50..2000 ms = 300
  pivotNote: slider 1..64 = 1
  target: slider 1200..12700 mc = 6400
  register: range 1200..12700 mc = [1200,12700]
Checked in 6 runs (every slider at its minimum and maximum, every option).
Score at the declared values (893 notes, 4 ms):
voice 1: 893 notes in 893 chords, 0-106906 ms, pitch 2300-6900

Sent. The panel: **gap** segments each voice into phrases; **pivotNote** (1–64) picks which note of every phrase anchors the shift — if a phrase is shorter, its last note is used; **target** (default E4) is where that pivot lands, the same for every phrase; **register** octave-folds any note that drifts out of range. Each phrase moves as a rigid block, preserving its internal intervals.
